newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget might not be enough for EMU - Employers.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget might not be enough for EMU - Employers.

text.p: The government's 1997 austerity budget might not be enough to push Italy into European economic and monetary union (EMU) from the outset, the director general of Italian employers' federation Confindustria said.

"We appreciate the effort being made but are not sure it will be enough," Innocenzo Cipolletta told a parliamentary committee, which is reviewing the budget package. "Too much of the part concerning new revenues has not been defined, and the element of uncertainty is too strong."
The government said the budget package would slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit.

Among the measures yet to be fully defined are 4.25 trillion lire worth of fresh income, which is expected to be largely drawn from value added tax hikes, and some 13 trillion lire, which will be raised from an unspecified "Euro-tax."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the budget will cut the ratio between Italy's deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) to three percent in 1997, as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty.
Cipolletta said he thought next year's deficit/GDP ratio would be 4.2 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
